families.axis: a single act of disrespect → conduct condemned as morally evil

members.tone: The flat, absolute name for conduct that offends morality, condemning without argument or degree.
Condemns the same conduct with preachy relish, as if the wrong were knowingly enjoyed, not just done: more vivid than the bare *evil*.
Frames the disrespect as a breach, something owed and transgressed, giving the act a hard formal weight that *irreverence* lacks.
The lightest blame here: an act that withholds due respect rather than one that breaks anything.

families.axis: bare absence of rudeness → the social forms actually observed

members.gloss: not rude; marked by satisfactory (or especially minimal) adherence to social usages and sufficient but not noteworthy consideration for others
members.tone: Approval at its lowest: it grants only that the manner was not rude, where *polite* can stretch to social rules kept well enough.

members.gloss: not rude; marked by satisfactory (or especially minimal) adherence to social usages and sufficient but not noteworthy consideration for others
members.tone: Credits the social rules as kept, not merely rudeness avoided.

flagged_for.sentence: Credits the social rules as kept

families.axis: a surface that merely shades the truth → a covering got up to misrepresent it

members.gloss: an outward or token appearance or form that is deliberately misleading
members.tone: British spelling of the same misleading surface: a respectable tint lent to something so it passes, only a tint, where *disguise* covers.

members.gloss: an outward or token appearance or form that is deliberately misleading
members.tone: The barest word here, naming only the outward or token form and leaving the deceit unsaid, where *pretence* puts the trick on show.

members.gloss: an outward or token appearance or form that is deliberately misleading
members.tone: A respectable-looking surface lent to something so it seems defensible; it does not hide the thing underneath, it only shades it.

members.gloss: an outward or token appearance or form that is deliberately misleading
members.tone: Carries the idea of a polish worked onto the outside, so the deceit is one of finish rather than of concealment as in *disguise*.

members.gloss: an outward semblance that misrepresents the true nature of something
members.tone: The most covering word here, not a shading of the truth but an outward form that actively misrepresents what lies under it.
British spelling, and it foregrounds the artfulness, naming the semblance as something got up rather than something merely appearing.
Like *pretence*, a cunning or faked appearance, but pictured as something put on and worn, so the deceit lies in taking it on.

families.axis: plainly suitable → propriety pushed past its purpose

members.tone: Warm approval - what accords with custom is credited with grace rather than mere compliance, unlike the dry *decorous*.
Gentle and pleased - it finds conduct agreeable in its accord with propriety rather than measuring it against a rule.
A phrase rather than a word, and formal to the point of ceremony - approval delivered by invoking the code instead of describing the conduct.
Cool and external - conduct is held up against a standard of propriety and passes, with none of the warmth of *becoming*.
Understated - grants that conduct accords with propriety without the ceremony *decorous* brings to the same verdict.
Approval as a verdict - the social rule was met, and nothing warmer than that is claimed.
The bluntest way to render the same social judgement as *correct*, carrying no formality at all.

members.gloss: in harmony with the spirit of particular persons or occasion
members.tone: Approval keyed to the occasion and the people in it rather than to any code - it praises harmony where *correct* praises compliance.

members.gloss: in harmony with the spirit of particular persons or occasion
members.tone: Modest and human - it grants that a thing suits the persons and the moment, with less deliberation than *fitting*.

members.gloss: proper or legitimate according to Muslim law
members.tone: A label, not praise: something is proper or legitimate under Muslim law, and the approval is the law's, not the speaker's.
Informal and reassuring - declares a thing proper or legitimate, above board and open to no objection.
Scornful: being too proper is taken as smugness, correct behaviour shown off as a mark of being better than others.
The mildest fault here: a sense of what is proper held so tightly it goes stiff, mocked rather than condemned.
Dismissive and faintly ridiculing - the overdone propriety is treated as fussiness, silly rather than severe like *priggish*.
Too proper to the point of being easily shocked, and so a harsher word than *prim*.
